pr_title: Fix writing `gh api -i` response headers to terminal pager
pr_body:
This ensures that `gh api` output streams are initialized _after_ the pager has been opened.

Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/6045

issue_context.title: `gh api` header flag `-i` does not work with check runs API
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

When using `gh api` with the flag to include headers `-i`, it does not display the headers.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Set up `gh api` with an auth token
1. Find a repo and get a check run id
1. Call `gh api -i /repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-runs/{id}`
1. Observe that no headers are shown in the output

### Expected vs actual behavior

- Expected (using `gh api -i /` as an example):

```X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
X-Frame-Options: deny
X-Github-Api-Version-Selected: 2022-08-09
X-Github-Media-Type: github.v3; format=json
...

{
  "current_user_url": "https://api.github.com/user",
  "current_user_authorizations_html_url": "https://github.com/settings/connections/applications{/client_id}",
  ...
}
```

- Actual: only the response content

### Notes

Further discussion can be found on [slack](https://github.slack.com/archives/CLLG3RMAR/p1659652754687339).

- Using `GH_DEBUG=api gh api ...` allows me to see the request headers, but not the response headers, and only after exiting the response
- Piping `gh api -i ...` to `cat` allows me to see all the headers
- @mislav mentions that this is a bug with the terminal pager and `gh api -i`

review_comments: Since `parseTemplate` uses `t.io` to determine if the output should be colored, it seems like there could be a case there the writer passed to `Execute` does not support colors where the one used when initializing the template does leading to weird output. This seems like a rare edge case though.
Good point. This could definitely be improved. Right now, I just wanted to be able to temporarily override the output writer without having to mutate the IOStreams object for this.
